logline: A man she turned down on a Saturday is standing in her office elevator on Monday — and the building is small.
format: silent live-action short, 12 hard cuts, no dialogue, no music, no on-screen text, for an external female narration track
look: large-format digital cinema, 50mm, shallow depth of field, natural skin texture, subtle 35mm film grain, muted natural colour, locked-off frames with exactly two very slow push-ins, no vignette, no filter, no slow motion

wardrobe.woman_office: pale sky-blue cotton blouse buttoned to the top, navy wide-leg trousers, plain black low-heel loafers, blank matte off-white plastic ID card on a thin black lanyard
wardrobe.woman_weekend: oatmeal-ivory chunky knit sweater, mid-blue straight jeans
wardrobe.man_office: white cotton shirt buttoned to the top, navy blazer, charcoal trousers, the identical blank ID card on the identical lanyard
wardrobe.man_weekend: charcoal-grey washed cotton shirt worn open over a white tee

F1.title: The man from the wine bar
F1.pov: the woman — she owns every close-up; the man is only ever seen through her
F1.intent: a weekend refusal comes back as a Monday colleague, and will not stop coming back
F1.audience: dry sympathetic cringe — the very specific horror of being recognised by someone you turned down, in a building you cannot leave
F1.device: object-as-actor (the blank ID lanyard proves the collision) + memory insert

contract.expect: the recognition lands as a physical freeze followed by a swallow, never as an expression; the final close-up curdles her politeness into fatigue
pass_bar: shot 1 shows only the blurred shoulder of the man, never his face
shots 2-5 play in weekend clothes, shots 6-12 in office clothes
the two ID cards match and stay blank
no mouth moves to speak at any point
no on-screen text, signage, logo or watermark anywhere
kill: the flashback plays in office clothes
the man's face is shown in shot 1
any spoken word or lip movement
a final smile that reads as flirtation
the memory frame announced by a blur, vignette or vintage filter

sound.ambient: none — complete silence; no room tone, no music, no effects, no voice

shots.beat: her eyes lock onto someone off frame right; her lids go still and she swallows once
shots.camera: locked-off, dead-centre eye level, 50mm, one very slow push-in of about 6% of the frame
shots.performance: unfocused gaze → pupils stop → chin lifts a millimetre → one swallow
shots.eyeline: off frame right, at the man's shoulder

shots.beat: he walks in and holds a phone out at chest height, screen toward her
shots.camera: locked-off from the far end of the bar counter, counter receding to frame right
shots.performance: a polite distance taken, then the phone lifted; lips closed

shots.beat: she gives one small decisive turn of the head, a closed-mouth smile
shots.performance: the smile reaches the mouth and not the eyes; fingers still on the glass stem
shots.eyeline: phone, then his face off frame

shots.beat: he does not leave — he lifts the phone again, half an inch higher, and holds it
shots.performance: a small hopeful question in the eyebrows; lips closed; absolute stillness after the lift

shots.beat: she refuses a second time, smaller; he turns away; her lips flatten and her eyes flick around the room
shots.transition_out: hard cut — from the memory back to now
shots.performance: eyes flick to the friend and back → a smaller shake → lips pressed → eyes lifting to check who saw

shots.beat: in the elevator her head turns up toward him and stops
shots.camera: locked-off from the side, both in profile facing the closed doors at frame left
shots.performance: stillness → the turn → the stop; shoulders never move

shots.beat: he drops his eyes to the floor and sets his jaw
shots.camera: locked-off in profile from her side
shots.performance: eyes down → jaw sets → one throat movement

shots.beat: two-shot: both stare at the doors between their two identical blank lanyards
shots.camera: locked-off, three-quarter from in front of them, she frame left, he frame right
shots.performance: no contact; the awkwardness lives in her tightened lips and his fixed stare
shots.eyeline: past each other at the doors

shots.beat: they cross paths in opposite directions with colleagues and only her pupils slide sideways
shots.camera: locked-off across the corridor, daylight from frame left
shots.performance: heads forward, no reaction but the eyes; colleagues oblivious

shots.beat: they meet eyes across two pickup points; she re-grips her cup, he half-smiles
shots.camera: locked-off at counter height, both in frame either side of the frame centre
shots.performance: eyes meet → her thumb finds the cup seam → his uncertain half-smile and a shallow nod

shots.beat: far apart down the lobby, each gives a shallow quick formal dip of the head
shots.camera: locked-off, deep perspective, she near frame left, he small at frame right
shots.performance: a bow that is over before it begins; no eye contact

shots.beat: her forced smile dies and the tired realisation settles in
shots.camera: locked-off, eye level, one very slow push-in of about 5%
shots.performance: straightens → smile goes out of the mouth → lips press → eyes narrow, brow knits a fraction; eyes stay open on nothing
shots.eyeline: off frame right into empty space
